requirements.requirement: Limit traffic from node2 toward node3 to 1 Mbit/s
requirements.summary: An Ansible playbook (site.yml) applied a tc tbf qdisc (rate 1Mbit) on node2's lan-a interface (enp8s0) toward node3. Direct iperf3 throughput tests from node2->node3 measured ~1.3-1.5 Mbit/s sender rate, consistent with the 1 Mbit/s cap, both before and after a node2 reboot (qdisc persisted via a systemd unit that reapplies it on boot).

requirements.requirement: Leave traffic from node3 toward node2 unrestricted
requirements.summary: node3's lan-b interface retained the default fq_codel qdisc (no shaping), and an explicit playbook task ensured no shaping qdisc was present. iperf3 from node3->node2 measured ~1.17 Gbit/s, confirming the reverse direction is unrestricted, and this held after node3's reboot as well.

requirements.requirement: Implement the traffic-shaping configuration using Ansible
requirements.summary: An ansible-playbook (/root/ansible-traffic-shaping/site.yml) was authored and executed against inventory targeting node1/node2/node3 from the ansible-controller node4; the shaping task ('Limit egress from node2 toward node3 to 1 Mbit/s'), the safety-net route tasks, and a persistence task were all applied via ansible-playbook runs that completed with changed/ok results and no failures.

overall_summary: The executor built an Ansible playbook that applies a tc tbf 1 Mbit/s egress shaper on node2's link toward node3 while leaving node3's link toward node2 at the default (unrestricted) qdisc, and validated the result with iperf3 bandwidth tests in both directions before and after rebooting node2 and node3, confirming persistence via a systemd unit. All three material outcomes (asymmetric 1 Mbit/s shaping, unrestricted reverse direction, Ansible-based implementation) are satisfied with direct, corroborating evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also executed across all four nodes with differing pre/post boot IDs and recovered connectivity/state, though the executor's own final report/evidence-selection metadata was essentially empty (placeholder 'test' values with an unresolved evidence command ID), so this evaluation relied entirely on the raw command timeline and fixed snapshots rather than the executor's self-reported evidence mapping.
limitations: The executor's final report and selected-evidence metadata contained only placeholder 'test' content and referenced an unresolved command ID (cmd-1), so no executor-curated evidence-to-requirement mapping was usable; this evaluation was built directly from the raw command timeline instead.

The playbook's full source (site.yml) was not directly visible in evidence - only base64-encoded content and ansible-playbook task/output logs - so implementation details beyond task names and observed effects could not be independently reviewed.

iperf3 throughput numbers were only sampled over short intervals (5-8s) rather than sustained, though they are consistent enough across multiple runs and both pre/post reboot to support high confidence.
Executor evidence item 1 referenced unknown command IDs: cmd-1

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were tied to establishing SSH/Ansible connectivity (necessary prerequisite for an unprepared cluster), configuring lan-a/lan-b addressing on node1 (necessary prerequisite for the routed topology), or collecting bounded final evidence (iperf tests, reboots). Two bounded, low-risk troubleshooting mutations were made and fully reverted: a temporary debug sshd instance on port 2222 on node1 (cmd-55af65d2ebd040ef, killed in cmd-85dc8b8b5fa74bea) and a test interface description on node1 eth0 (cmd-b59dd7b02c1548a6, deleted in cmd-888464970ec44fd5). iperf3 was installed via apt on node2 and node3 for bandwidth verification (cmd-fcc8e98e31a041e3, cmd-e8c9b7e1f1ab4ed2) and left installed, and a small log file /tmp/iperf_final.log remained on node3 - minor, low-risk residue directly tied to evidence collection rather than unrelated scope creep. No failed or conflicting services, no damaged package state, and no weakened security controls were observed in the final state.
